title: Q3 2026 Lithium Price Review
gist: Lithium carbonate, hydroxide and spodumene fell roughly 19-24% in Q3 2026 as Jianxiawo supply disruption was overwhelmed by Australian restarts, Chinese policy headwinds and a September inventory-data scare that Benchmark argues overshot fundamentals.

insights.claim: Battery-grade lithium carbonate (EXW China) fell 20.8% in Q3 2026 to RMB127,750/tonne (USD19,025/tonne), extending the correction that began in Q2.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Sets the current price level and confirms a second straight quarterly decline.

insights.claim: Lithium hydroxide (EXW China) dropped 19.2% in Q3 2026 to RMB120,000/tonne (USD17,875/tonne), and FOB Australia spodumene concentrate fell 23.5% to USD17,000/tonne.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Feedstock fell faster than chemicals, squeezing miner margins relative to converters.

insights.claim: Q3 lithium pricing was volatile: a decline through July, an August rally, then a sharp September reversal that erased the quarter's gains within days.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Quarterly endpoints mask intra-quarter swings; sentiment-driven moves can reverse quickly.

insights.claim: Seaborne Asia, Europe and North America carbonate prices lagged the Chinese decline by several weeks, a transmission pattern seen throughout 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: China price moves lead ex-China prices, so Chinese prints are an early signal for other regions.
insights.locator: Why did lithium prices keep falling through Q3?

insights.claim: CATL's Jianxiawo mine, after securing a safety production permit at end-Q2, resumed informally in July but bypassed an unresolved tailings pond dispute, drew more than 70 formal complaints, and halted again in early August.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Regulatory and community friction makes Jianxiawo restarts unreliable as a supply source.
insights.locator: What happened to CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Q3?

insights.claim: By early September regulators revoked Jianxiawo's environmental impact assessment entirely, forcing CATL to restart the review and returning the mine to care and maintenance.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Removes a swing supply source from China's near-term balance.
insights.locator: What happened to CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Q3?

insights.claim: Benchmark cut its 2026 Jianxiawo mined output forecast by nearly half and warns the review could stretch into Q4 or even 2027.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Supply-side support for prices depends on how long the review lasts.
insights.locator: Benchmark cut its 2026 mined output forecast

insights.claim: Tightening Jianxiawo supply plus more converters than usual undergoing maintenance drove Chinese carbonate higher through late August, to RMB142,000/tonne by 2 September.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Shows how quickly prices respond to Chinese supply headlines and converter downtime.

insights.claim: Mineral Resources restarted Bald Hill after an 18-month suspension and Core Lithium resumed operations at Finniss, adding to Q2 resumptions at Ngungaju, Pioneer Dome and Mt Marion.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Restarting hard-rock supply caps upside in spodumene and adds to feedstock pressure.
insights.locator: How did Australian restarts and Chinese demand policy impact lithium prices?

insights.claim: China moved toward confirming removal of a domestic battery tax exemption, which Benchmark had flagged as speculation at end-Q2, adding downstream margin pressure while feedstock arrivals increased.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Policy-driven margin squeeze at cell makers can reduce their willingness to pay for lithium.
insights.quote: This added a fresh source of downstream margin pressure just as the market was absorbing additional feedstock arrivals
insights.locator: On the demand side, China moved toward confirming

insights.claim: The Chinese government aimed to counteract overcapacity in the cell and LFP cathode sectors, and announced a pause on new ESS and later EV cell capacity expansion approvals.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Capping downstream capacity growth tempers future lithium demand growth expectations.
insights.locator: Chinese domestic carbonate rose at the start of July; Additionally, the Chinese government announced a pause

insights.claim: September cell production schedules showed NCM cathode output plans slowing month-on-month while LFP rose only modestly, and Benchmark calls sluggish NCM schedules a genuine source of demand weakness that could further weigh on hydroxide prices.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Hydroxide is more exposed than carbonate to weak NCM demand.
insights.locator: Cell production scheduling data for September

insights.claim: Market rumours that several cell buyers were shifting orders away from CATL to rival battery suppliers added to bearish sentiment in September.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Unconfirmed; watch whether it becomes verified order losses.

insights.claim: On 16 September EXW China carbonate fell 7.3% and CIF Asia spot carbonate fell 11.9% after a Chinese third-party data provider sharply revised up its lithium inventory estimate, a change later revealed to be primarily methodological.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A data-methodology change triggered the quarter's biggest move, showing prices are vulnerable to inventory-data headlines.
insights.locator: Why did prices crash in mid-September?

insights.claim: The inventory revision shook trader confidence and led long contract holders on futures exchanges to unwind positions, while Benchmark's Inventory Tracker China showed consistent chemical destocking throughout the quarter.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Divergence between destocking data and price weakness suggests the September selloff was positioning-driven, not fundamental.
insights.quote: Nonetheless, the change shook trader confidence and spurred long contract holders on futures exchanges to unwind their positions
insights.locator: Why did prices crash in mid-September?

insights.claim: Benchmark's principal lithium price analyst argues that Q3 was defined by genuine ore supply disruption followed by an inventory and demand scare that dominated late-quarter pricing despite strong fundamentals.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Benchmark's view is that the late-quarter weakness overshoots fundamentals.
insights.quote: The latter ultimately dominated price action into the end of the quarter, despite fundamentals remaining strong.

insights.claim: Benchmark's Q4 base case assumes Jianxiawo's environmental review concludes within Q4, with slippage into 2027 flagged as a risk.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Timing of the review is a key swing factor for Chinese supply and price direction.
insights.locator: What could impact lithium prices in Q4 2026?

insights.claim: Continued pressure on feedstock prices could render currently marginal DSO shipments uneconomic.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Marginal DSO supply exiting would provide a floor under feedstock prices.

insights.claim: Benchmark states fundamentals do not support the recent bearish sentiment holding through year-end, and treats a sentiment reversal as a Q4 factor.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Implies potential rebound risk for short positions if sentiment normalizes.
